hint.text: Im Begriff Identity Politics bündelt sich eine Vielzahl öffentlicher Debatten und politischer Bewegungen, die in den letzten Jahren großen gesellschaftlichen Einfluss hatten.
hint.label: Context

atoms.b: Identity politics describe the political alliance and activism of ((oppressed)) groups based on their ((common)) identity. Some of these groups are Black people, Indigenous people, Hispanic people, Muslims, Jews, (formerly) ((colonised)) peoples, Feminists, the LGBTQ+ community, disabled people and other minority groups. While acknowledging the ((different)) forms of discrimination each group may face, it remains important to consider ((intersectionality)).

instruction.text: Is this an argument for or against Identity Politics?

atoms.a:
Ongoing Discrimination

Discrimination persists through institutions, policies and laws that reproduce unequal treatment, and through prejudices and social norms.

feedback.wrong: Identity Politics is an effective tool in the fight against ongoing discrimination.

atoms.a:
Oversimplifying Identities

Boxing people into fixed categories and ignoring differences within groups, can reinforce prejudice and limit how individuals are seen or heard.

feedback.wrong: Identity Politics can fail to serve individuals or reproduce prejudice by only focussing on groups and labels.

atoms.a:
Addressing Needs

Different social groups have different needs. These are shaped by a group's access to resources and their lived experience. Advocating for an inclusive society is important.

feedback.wrong: Identity Politics can advocate for a group's specific needs.

atoms.a:
Equal but not the same

Equality means all people deserve dignity but not that all people are the same. If social disadvantages are ignored, policies will continue to benefit majorities while minorities remain disadvantaged.

feedback.wrong: Identity Politics can help to advocate for equality and inclusion which takes into account natural and social differences between people.

atoms.a:
Finding Solidarity

Disadvantaged groups can form positive collective identities, as a way to affirm dignity and resist marginalisation.

hint.sound: <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>solidarity</lang> bedeutet Solidarität oder Zusammenhalt. <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>to affirm</lang> bedeutet bestätigen.
hint.label: Vocabulary

feedback.wrong: Identity Politics can create a positive self understanding within a minority group.

atoms.a:
Addressing the broader perspective

A focus on specific identities can lead to a loss of broader perspective, and wider societal issues risk being overlooked.

feedback.wrong: By focussing on differences Identity Politics might fail to take intersectionality into account or fail to address overarching issues.

finish.text: Identity Politics can help to highlight specific inequalities and give marginalized groups a voice, ensuring that policies address the needs of all people, not just the majority. However, a focus on division and loss in details might hinder productive change.
